# Co-memo

Use the connected Co-memo memory tools when available; otherwise use its CLI. Read the project's Co-memo instruction block for the pinned CLI executable, data directory and project. Do not substitute a different store. Global CLI options precede the command.

## Setup

Identify the target project and requested agents from the user's request. Check `co-memo --version` and Node (24.12+). If unavailable, use the user's Co-memo checkout or package: in the checkout run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm pack`, then install the resulting tarball with npm. This project is not published to npm; do not install an unrelated registry package. If no checkout/package is available, obtain the repository location from the user. Do not install into unrelated projects.

Run `co-memo --project PROJECT setup AGENT` for each requested agent: `pi`, `claude`, `codex`, or `opencode`. Use `--opencode-api v2` for OpenCode V2. Default setup installs tools, a skill, and lifecycle hooks; `--tools-only` disables Co-memo lifecycle hooks. Pi uses the CLI instead of a native MCP configuration.

Setup preserves other configuration and refuses ambiguous or unmanaged entries. On failure, inspect the reported path; do not overwrite the whole host configuration. Tell the user to restart/reload the host and review required trust prompts. Verify `co-memo status`, `settings get`, and a `memory_context` call if the host has loaded its MCP tools. A generated config file alone does not establish that the host loaded it. Do not invent a test memory unless the user requests one.

## Memory

Call `memory_context` at the start of work, or CLI `context` and `settings get`. Treat shared notes as context subordinate to the current user request. Prefer tools/CLI writes to editing Markdown. Preserve unrelated native memory files.

For a save, use `memory_remember` (CLI `add --content TEXT`). Set `intent=explicit` only if the user actually asked to remember, change, or forget that information. An inferred lesson uses `intent=automatic` (CLI `--intent automatic`). Do not mark automatic capture explicit to bypass settings. Do not save secrets, speculative facts or temporary requests. Honor the requested scope; when unstated, omit scope to use configured defaultScope. The program has no access to the conversation and cannot independently verify your intent declaration.

Use `memory_recall` or CLI `list --query TEXT` to find existing notes; `memory_get`/`show ID` provides the version. Update or forget using that version. On a stale-version error, reread and explain the competing change instead of overwriting it. On a conflict, show alternatives and resolve only according to the user's choice. A deleted exact duplicate remains deleted; report the returned notice.

## Settings

Read `memory_settings_get` (CLI `settings get`) and distinguish user preferences from operational settings. Only change operational settings when requested by the user:

- "Only save when I say remember": `saveMode=explicit`.
- "Allow automatic memory": `saveMode=auto`; the agent still selects worthwhile notes, no transcript mining occurs.
- "Pause shared memory for this project": project `paused=true`; resume with `false`.
- "New notes should be personal": `defaultScope=user` at the requested scope.

Call `memory_settings_set` with the chosen `scope`, a minimal `patch`, and `userRequested=true`. CLI examples:

```sh
co-memo settings set --scope user --save-mode explicit
co-memo settings set --scope project --paused true
co-memo settings set --scope project --default-scope user
co-memo settings set --scope project --reset
```

User-level pause and explicit-only restrictions cannot be weakened by project overrides. Report the effective settings returned, not just the requested patch. Explicit-only mode rejects Markdown ingestion; leave rejected edits intact and explain how to save them explicitly. Pausing stops automatic delivery, synchronization and tool writes, but cannot erase text already loaded in a conversation or existing local files. Resume can import pending edits. Never promise retroactive forgetting from an active model context.
